question.text: What will be the highest significant wave height at NDBC buoy 46026 (18 NM west of San Francisco) on November 26, 2026 (UTC)?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the highest value in the WVHT (significant wave height, in meters) column of the NDBC station 46026 realtime standard meteorological data file (https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/data/realtime2/46026.txt) among all rows whose timestamp (YY MM DD hh mm, UTC) falls on November 26, 2026, i.e. timestamps from 00:00 through 23:50 UTC on that date. For example, if the largest WVHT entry on that date reads 3.4, the question resolves to 3.4 m; if the largest reads 4.1, it resolves to 4.1 m. Rows in which WVHT is reported as "MM" are treated as missing and ignored. Only station 46026 (SAN FRANCISCO – 18NM West of San Francisco, CA, 37.750 N 122.838 W) is used, and no smoothing, averaging, or unit conversion is applied to the file's WVHT values.
question.fine_print: Resolution uses the realtime data file as it stands when the question resolves; later quality-controlled revisions of the same observations do not change the outcome. If the buoy reports no valid WVHT value at all for November 26, 2026 (for example, a sensor or mooring outage), the question will be annulled. If the realtime file itself is inaccessible, the same NDBC 46026 WVHT observations as published on other NDBC pages or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used.

research:
I found nothing that settles this yet. The answer depends on weather 10 days out, and the season so far is far rougher than recent years. The buoy reached about 7.0 m on Nov 14 and 6.5 m early on Nov 16. On Nov 26 in 2021-2025 it peaked between about 1.5 and 2.9 m.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The realtime file at https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/data/realtime2/46026.txt is live. It holds 6,470 rows, from 2026-10-02 to 2026-11-16 18:10 UTC. The latest WVHT is 4.2 m (18:10 UTC), with an average period of 10.3 s from 276°, and 4.4 m at 17:50. [NDBC realtime](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/data/realtime2/46026.txt)
- Oddity: the file shows water temperature (WTMP) of about 18.5 °C, which is unusually warm for November here. The wave data look normal.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet; it depends on conditions about 10 days out.
- The buoy is reporting normally, with WVHT every 10 to 20 minutes and some "MM" (missing) gaps. I found no sign of an outage.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16, 10:24 AM PST: The NWS San Francisco forecast discussion says seas ease Tuesday afternoon, then "build again by Wednesday with larger swells arriving." It expects gale gusts and thunderstorms midweek, and another system "starting Saturday" (Nov 21), with no details given. [NWS AFD](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=MTR&issuedby=MTR&product=AFD)
- 2026-11-16: Buoy readings sampled at 3-hour intervals:
  - Nov 16: 3.9 m (00:20), 5.0 (03:20), 6.5 (06:20), 6.0 (09:20), 4.8 (12:20 and 15:20).
  - Nov 15: 3.1 to 4.3 m.
  - Nov 14: 3.8 (00:20), 6.0 (06:20), 7.0 (12:20), 6.8 (15:20), 6.1 (18:20), 5.2 (21:20). The true peak may be higher, because I only sampled.
  - [NDBC](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/data/realtime2/46026.txt)
- 2026-11-14/15: The Nov 14-15 swell hit the coast. News reports say NWS measured waves over 30 ft at Monterey and Point Reyes, buoy 46042 read 32 ft at 21 s, and a buoy off Point Reyes recorded 9.5 m, its highest since 2015. Reports also mention a "super El Niño." [NY Post](https://nypost.com/2026/11/14/us-news/massive-waves-up-to-60-feet-threaten-northern-california-coast-as-nws-issues-urgent-warning/), [Lodi News](https://www.lodinews.com/news/national/article_e346de5a-256e-5f98-a080-b13943ca60b1.html)
- 2026-11-10: NWS was quoted saying "Seven or eight pulses of energy are possible through the week of Thanksgiving." [GovTech/SF Chronicle](https://www.govtech.com/em/biggest-waves-in-years-to-slam-californias-coast)
- Undated, about 1 day old: an SF Chronicle headline says "another round of mammoth waves within days," with 40-55 ft maximum individual waves "Wednesday evening into Thursday morning." That most likely means Nov 18-19, not Nov 25-26. The page would not load, so I could not check. [SF Chronicle](https://www.sfchronicle.com/weather/article/waves-tide-california-bay-area-coast-22531154.php)

## 4. Base rates
Highest WVHT at 46026 on Nov 26 in past years. 2025 is the full-day maximum; 2021-2024 are 4-hourly samples, so the true maxima are slightly higher.
- 2025: 1.49 m, a calm day of 0.7-1.5 m. [NDBC 2025](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/view_text_file.php?filename=46026h2025.txt.gz&dir=data/historical/stdmet/)
- 2024: about 2.5 m, falling from 2.48 to 1.4. [NDBC 2024](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/view_text_file.php?filename=46026h2024.txt.gz&dir=data/historical/stdmet/)
- 2023: about 2.9 m (2.1-2.92). [NDBC 2023](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/view_text_file.php?filename=46026h2023.txt.gz&dir=data/historical/stdmet/)
- 2022: about 2.3 m (1.8-2.33). [NDBC 2022](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/view_text_file.php?filename=46026h2022.txt.gz&dir=data/historical/stdmet/)
- 2021: about 2.0 m (1.4-1.97). [NDBC 2021](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/view_text_file.php?filename=46026h2021.txt.gz&dir=data/historical/stdmet/)

Seasonal comparison:
- The past 5 years span about 1.5 to 2.9 m, with a median near 2.3 m.
- This year is running far above them: 3-7 m on Nov 13-16, against early-October values of about 1.3 m.
- Values swing a lot day to day. Nov 14-15 alone went from 7.0 down to 3.1 m.
- I did not pull mid-November values for earlier years, so I can't compare each year's change from Nov 16 to Nov 26.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or Metaculus question on buoy wave heights.
- The Kalshi markets listed are unrelated (elections, ballot measures, test scores). The one loosely related is San Francisco November rainfall: "Above 6 inches" is priced at 0.54 and "Above 8 inches" at 0.24. Those prices point to a very wet, stormy month.

## 6. Upcoming events and latest official forecasts
NWS coastal waters forecast for Point Reyes to Pigeon Point, 10-60 NM out, issued 2026-11-16 10:05 AM PST (offshore of the buoy, which sits about 18 NM out):

- A Gale Watch is in effect for Tuesday night.
- [NWS CWF](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=MTR&issuedby=MTR&product=CWF)

Beyond that:
- Another system is expected from about Sat Nov 21. [NWS AFD](https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=MTR&issuedby=MTR&product=AFD)
- Reporting says NWS flags a higher risk of heavy precipitation and strong winds around Nov 25-27, and that storms could line up with king tides. CPC favors above-normal precipitation for Thanksgiving week. I could not read the source articles. [SF Chronicle](https://www.sfchronicle.com/weather-forecast/article/rain-storm-weather-san-francisco-california-22529476.php), [Country Herald](https://countryherald.com/california/sacramento/northern-california-thanksgiving-weather-rain-mountain-snow-risk-nov-22-28)
- I found no official wave forecast for Nov 26 itself. The NWS forecast ends Nov 20.
- Things to check before the forecast closes: WaveWatch III/GFS-Wave runs covering Nov 26, plus CDIP and Surfline long-range outlooks.

Other search results: [Active NorCal](https://www.activenorcal.com/the-biggest-waves-in-years-set-to-slam-northern-california-starting-tonight/), [Surfer](https://www.surfer.com/news/40-foot-california-swell-el-nino).

## 4. Base rates
Daily maximum on Nov 26 in past years, from the NDBC historical files (2-decimal values):
- 2025-11-26: about 1.5 m, from readings every 3 hours (1.45 at 00:10, dropping to 0.83). A calm day. [NDBC 2025](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/view_text_file.php?filename=46026h2025.txt.gz&dir=data/historical/stdmet/)
- 2024-11-26: 2.53 m. I checked every reading that day; the range was 1.36-2.53. [NDBC 2024](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/view_text_file.php?filename=46026h2024.txt.gz&dir=data/historical/stdmet/)
- 2023-11-26: about 2.9 m from 3-hourly readings (top value 2.92). [NDBC 2023](https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/view_text_file.php?filename=46026h2023.txt.gz&dir=data/historical/stdmet/)

Takeaways:
- In those four years, Nov 26 maxima were about 1.5-2.9 m, with a median near 2.5 m. The 3-hourly figures are lower bounds.
- This year is running well above those years. Mid-November 2026 daily maxima were 3-7 m, against roughly 1.5-3 m in a typical year.
- Day-to-day swings are big: the buoy went from 3.8 m to 7.0 m in about 16 hours on Nov 13-14, then fell to about 3 m within 24 hours.
- I did not pull a full climatology of Nov 16 to Nov 26 changes, and I did not check 2021.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The outcome will be known about 11 days from now. Nov 26 data will be complete by Nov 27, and the question resolves around Nov 27 18:00 UTC. That is far beyond the range of any skillful deterministic wave forecast.

(b) **Latest known value:** 4.2 m at 18:10 UTC on 2026-11-16 (4.4 m at 17:50). Recent peaks were about 7.0 m on Nov 14 and 6.5 m on Nov 16.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 4.2 m. Daily maxima in a stormy pattern like this run around 4 to 5 m.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** The trend is a series of large swell pulses, with a big one around Nov 18-19 and seas easing to 6-8 ft (about 2 m) on Nov 20. Another system follows from Nov 21, and Nov 25-27 is flagged for heavy rain and wind. On that pattern the Nov 26 maximum would be roughly 3 to 4 m.

(e) **Historical variation:** Daily maxima swing widely within days. Nov 14 to 15 went from 7.0 m down to 3.1 m. The Nov 26 maxima for 2021-2025 ranged from 1.5 to 2.9 m (median about 2.3 m). Over 10 days, the value essentially resets to climatology conditioned on the regime.

(f) **Experts and markets:**
- An NWS forecaster was quoted on Nov 10 saying "seven or eight pulses of energy" were possible through Thanksgiving week.
- NWS reportedly flags elevated storm and wind risk for Nov 25-27, and CPC favors a wet Thanksgiving week.
- Kalshi prices about a 54% chance of more than 6 inches of November rain in San Francisco, which points to a very active month.
- No market exists on wave height itself.

Taken together, I shift the climatological median of about 2.3-2.5 m up to about 3.0 m.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** A ridge builds over Thanksgiving, with light winds and a small, decaying swell. The daily maximum is about 1.3-1.6 m, like 2025.
- **High:** A deep low arrives on Nov 26, combining strong south or west winds with a large northwest groundswell. Seas reach 6-7 m or more, as on Nov 14.

**Tail scenarios behind the extreme percentiles:**
- **1st percentile:** a flat, post-ridge day with leftover small swell, around 1.2 m.
- **99th percentile:** a repeat of the Nov 14 event landing on Nov 26, around 7.2 m.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: a ridge builds and a calm lull sets in with only small residual swell and light winds. The daily maximum could be around 1.3-1.6 m, as on November 26, 2025.
- High: a strong storm hits around November 26, with a powerful nearby low bringing gale-force wind sea on top of a large northwest groundswell. That could push WVHT to 6-7.5 m, similar to November 14.
